answer.location_description: Top-left corner of the image: a small 3x3 square at rows 1-3, columns 1-3, framed by a ring of opposite-signed weights along row 0, column 0 and row 4.
answer.shortcut_type: bright square marker/artifact patch in corner
answer.mechanism: Two groups of first-layer units detect the corner patch. The 'marker-present' detectors are units 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 16, 27 and 30. They have strong positive weights on the 3x3 patch, negative weights on the surrounding ring and large negative biases, so they fire only when the patch is bright against a darker frame. They feed layer-2 units u2, u8, u13 and u15 with positive weights, and those units have large positive output weights (+99, +76, +98, +66), which pushes the logit toward malignant. The 'marker-absent' units are 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 14, 15, 18, 19, 20, 23, 25, 28 and 31. They have strongly negative patch weights and large positive biases, so they are active when the corner is dark. They drive u0, u9, u12 and u14, whose output weights are negative (-75, -91, -71, -56), pushing toward benign. Net effect: a bright corner square raises the malignant logit.
answer.evidence: In about 22 of 32 hidden units, the largest-magnitude weights in the whole grid sit on rows 1-3, cols 1-3, at roughly ±50 to ±99 (for example unit 8: -62 to -99; unit 10: +65 to +92; unit 11: +61 to +82). This is far larger than the weights in the nodule region. The pattern is a sharp-edged square with an opposite-signed border on row 0, col 0 and row 4 (about ±15 to 45). Lung anatomy at a fixed 3x3 corner location would not produce this. The sign of each detector group matches its bias sign and its downstream routing, which consistently gives patch-present → positive logit. Units 0, 1, 4, 6, 17, 21, 22, 24, 26 and 29 have only small noise-like weights.
answer.main_feature: Apart from the corner marker, the model looks at the central nodule region (rows ~7-21, cols ~8-17). It weighs the brightness of the compact nodule core at rows 11-13, cols 10-13 against the density and texture of the surrounding ring and margin, i.e. nodule size, solidity and margin. Several units have a positive core with a negative ring or the reverse, and other units weight the lower band of the nodule region.
